exercises.prompt: What is taharah about?
exercises.explanation: Taharah means ritual purity: removing impurity (najasah) and the state that wudu or ghusl fixes.

source.text: And purify your clothing.

options.text: Avoiding all contact with dust and soil
Being clean and free from anything that blocks valid worship
Keeping only the face and hands clean

exercises.prompt: The Prophet called cleanliness "half of faith". What does that mean for daily life?
exercises.explanation: Taharah is not a formality - it is worship itself: the same care you give your body is counted as faith.

source.text: Cleanliness is half of faith.

options.text: Cleanliness matters only inside a mosque
Keeping body, clothes and surroundings clean is a major part of the religion
Only clothes must be clean before prayer
Washing more than three times is always better

exercises.prompt: Your shirt has a small stain of urine from a child you carried. What is the ruling mindset?
exercises.explanation: Najasah is ritual impurity; cleaning it is required before prayer is valid in that garment.

source.text: The Prophet washed the urine of a child with water.

options.text: Treat it as najasah - clean the area before praying in it
Ignore it, it will dry out

exercises.prompt: When does wudu matter most?
exercises.explanation: Allah commands wudu when you rise to pray: purity is the gateway to standing before Him.

source.text: O you who believe, when you rise to pray, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows.

options.text: Before the ritual prayer and when handling the Quran (per most scholars)

exercises.prompt: Arrange the steps of wudu in the correct order.
exercises.explanation: Wudu follows the order the Quran and the Prophet (peace be upon him) described: hands, mouth, nose, face, forearms, head, ears, feet.

source.text: Uthman ibn Affan called for water and performed ablution, washing each part three times, then said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah perform ablution like this."

steps.text: Wash both hands up to the wrists three times
Wash the forearms up to the elbows three times
Wipe the head once with wet hands
Wash the feet up to the ankles three times

exercises.prompt: You are about to perform wudu. What do you say as you begin?
exercises.explanation: In the name of Allah (before wudu). (Bismillah). Said at the start of wudu; the Prophet said there is no (complete) wudu for the one who does not mention Allah’s name.

source.text: There is no wudu for the one who does not mention the name of Allah upon it.

options.text: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.
In the name of Allah (before wudu).
All praise is for Allah who fed us, gave us drink, and made us Muslims.
May Allah guide you and set your affairs right.

exercises.prompt: You have just completed wudu. What do you say?
exercises.explanation: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. (Ashhadu an la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh). Said after completing wudu; the eight gates of Paradise are opened for the one who says it.

source.text: Whoever performs wudu and says this, the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him.

options.text: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.
In the name of Allah (before wudu).
O Allah, I seek refuge in You from male and female devils.
All praise is for Allah who gave us life after death, and to Him is the return.

exercises.prompt: Which parts are wiped with wet hands rather than washed?
exercises.explanation: The Quran orders washing for the face, arms and feet, and wiping (mas-h) for the head; the ears share the head’s ruling.

source.text: Wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows, wipe over your heads, and wash your feet to the ankles.

exercises.prompt: How many times did the Prophet commonly wash each limb in wudu?
exercises.explanation: Uthman described the Prophet’s wudu washing each part three times - the middle path of the Sunnah.

source.text: Uthman performed ablution washing each part three times, then said: I saw the Messenger of Allah perform ablution like this.

exercises.prompt: What did the Prophet say after finishing wudu?
exercises.explanation: The shahada dua after wudu is the full-circle moment: purification ends with a testimony of faith.

source.text: Whoever performs wudu and says the shahada, the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him.

options.text: The shahada dua - and the eight gates of Paradise open for it

exercises.prompt: What is said at the start of wudu?
exercises.explanation: Beginning with Allah’s name is a small habit with a big reward attached to wudu.

source.text: There is no wudu for the one who does not mention the name of Allah upon it.

exercises.prompt: Why does deep sleep while lying down break wudu, while light dozing while seated may not?
exercises.explanation: The issue is not sleep itself but awareness: deep sleep while lying down removes the certainty needed for wudu’s validity.

source.text: The Companions waited for the Prophet to wake for prayer; deep sleep was treated as breaking wudu.

options.text: Because lying down is always impure
Because the bed may be dirty
Because full awareness of bodily control is lost

exercises.prompt: Which of these does NOT break wudu?
exercises.explanation: Wudu breaks by what leaves the body or by losing awareness in deep sleep - simple washing never breaks it.

source.text: The Prophet distinguished acts that require renewal of wudu from ordinary daily actions.

options.text: Washing your hands for a meal

exercises.prompt: Which of these breaks wudu?
exercises.explanation: Anything exiting from the front or back passage breaks wudu - the classic case is using the toilet.

source.text: Wudu is broken by what exits from the two passages.

exercises.prompt: You feel a faint sensation after praying but are 90% sure it is nothing. What do you rely on?
exercises.explanation: Doubt does not break certainty: the Prophet said one should not leave prayer for a mere doubt until hearing a sound or smelling an odor.

source.text: He should not leave (the prayer) until he hears a sound or smells an odor.

options.text: You repeat wudu every time you doubt
Certainty - wudu stays valid until breaking it is certain

exercises.prompt: You are travelling with no water after using the toilet. What do you do?
exercises.explanation: Impurity must be removed; where water is unavailable, clean dry material serves the purpose, and tayammum covers the wudu need.

source.text: The Prophet allowed cleaning with stones (dry material) when water was scarce.

options.text: Leave it until you find water days later
Clean yourself with whatever pure dry material is available until the impurity is gone

exercises.prompt: Which habits did the Prophet list as part of the natural fitrah?
exercises.explanation: These are the everyday hygiene habits of the fitrah - Islam builds cleanliness into routine.

source.text: The fitrah includes clipping the moustache, trimming nails and cleaning the private parts with water.

options.text: Trimming the moustache, cleaning after the toilet, cutting nails and using the siwak

exercises.prompt: Why did the Prophet stress the miswak so much?
exercises.explanation: The Prophet wished he could make the miswak obligatory at every prayer - purity of the mouth is worship hygiene.

source.text: Were it not that I would burden my community, I would have ordered them to use the miswak with every prayer.

options.text: It is required before every meal
It cleans the mouth that remembers Allah and recites His book

exercises.prompt: What is istinja?
exercises.explanation: Istinja is basic dignity hygiene and was practiced by the Prophet - it removes impurity right at its source.

source.text: The Prophet used water for istinja and taught the Companions to do so.

options.text: Cleaning yourself with water after using the toilet

exercises.prompt: Arrange the steps of tayammum in the correct order.
exercises.explanation: Tayammum replaces wudu or ghusl when water is unavailable or harmful: one strike of clean earth, then wipe the face and the hands.

source.text: If you are ill or on a journey... and you do not find water, then strike clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it.

steps.text: Strike clean earth lightly with both palms
Wipe the backs of the hands up to the wrists

exercises.prompt: When is ghusl required?
exercises.explanation: Ghusl is the full purifying bath for major impurity - and Islam makes it accessible: the Quran’s command is followed by the concession of tayammum when water is not usable.

source.text: If you are in a state of major impurity, purify yourselves; but if you are ill or... do not find water, then strike clean earth.

options.text: In states of major impurity, such as after a wet dream or after a woman’s menses end

exercises.prompt: What do you strike for tayammum?
exercises.explanation: The Quran says "clean earth (sa’id tayyib)" - any natural pure dusty surface works.

source.text: Then strike clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it.

options.text: Clean earth or a dusty, pure surface

exercises.prompt: When is tayammum allowed?
exercises.explanation: Tayammum is Allah’s concession: no one is trapped without a path to prayer.

source.text: If you are ill or on a journey... and you do not find water, then strike clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it.

options.text: Whenever it is faster than wudu
When water is unavailable or unusable, or illness makes using it harmful

exercises.prompt: Which parts are wiped in tayammum?
exercises.explanation: One strike, two wipes: the face and the hands - simpler than wudu, same purpose.

source.text: Wipe your faces and hands with it.

options.text: The arms up to the elbows
